observed.panel:
CSYNC synchronization versus CDS / CDNSKEY DS intent

CSYNC requests NS and address/glue synchronization. It does not request DS replacement. CDS and CDNSKEY instead express child intent for the parent DS set.

CSYNC - NS/glue synchronization
Signed child request to synchronize eligible NS/address data; never a DS-change authorization. CSYNC - NS/glue synchronization source 1 CSYNC - NS/glue synchronization source 2
CDS - proposed DS intent
Child-published management intent; parent DS publication is a separate checked action. CDS - proposed DS intent source 1 CDS - proposed DS intent source 2 CDS - proposed DS intent source 3 CDS - proposed DS intent source 4 CDS - proposed DS intent source 5 CDS - proposed DS intent source 6
CDNSKEY - public-key intent for DS
Child-published public-key management signal, not an already published parent DS. CDNSKEY - public-key intent for DS source 1 CDNSKEY - public-key intent for DS source 2 CDNSKEY - public-key intent for DS source 3 CDNSKEY - public-key intent for DS source 4 CDNSKEY - public-key intent for DS source 5 CDNSKEY - public-key intent for DS source 6

The parent independently authenticates eligible records and applies its processing policy. CSYNC never authorizes a DS change; CDS/CDNSKEY intent is not acceptance or publication of parent DS records.
observed.sourceLabel: CDNSKEY - public-key intent for DS source 6
